newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan buys record $22.74 bln US car parts in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Japan buys record $22.74 bln US car parts in 96/97.

text.p: The Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association (JAMA) said on Thursday that purchases of U.S. car parts by Japanese vehicle makers rose to a record $22.74 billion in the year that ended on March 31, 1997, up 8.1 percent from the previous record of $21.03 billion in 1995/96.
JAMA also said that purchases of European Union-made car parts by Japanese vehicle makers totalled $5.95 billion in 1996/97, up 5.2 percent from $5.66 billion the year before.

Purchases of U.S. car parts and materials in 1996/97 included $19.05 billion worth for use at Japanese makers' U.S. plants, up 7.9 percent from the year before, and $3.69 billion for use in plants in Japan, up 9.2 percent, JAMA said in a statement.

Purchases of EU-made car parts and materials in 1996/97 included $5.15 billion worth for use at Japanese makers' plants in EU countries, up 5.6 percent from the previous year, and $803 million worth for use in plants in Japan, up 2.6 percent.

In January 1992, when then U.S. President George Bush visited Tokyo with the heads of the U.S. "Big Three" carmakers, the Japanese car industry set a target of more than doubling its purchases of U.S.-made car parts and materials to $19 billion in fiscal 1994 from $9 billion in 1990.

After the target period expired, Tokyo and Washington reached an historic pact in June 1995 to open up Japan's car and car parts market to more foreign competition, but this did not specify targets for Tokyo's purchases of U.S.-made car parts.
